newsitem.title: USA: NHL-KAMENSKY GOAL IN OT HELPS AVALANCHE END PENS' WIN STREAK.
newsitem.headline: NHL-KAMENSKY GOAL IN OT HELPS AVALANCHE END PENS' WIN STREAK.

text.p: Valeri Kamensky scored at 3:55 of overtime to give the visiting Colorado Avalanche a 4-3 victory Thursday and end the 14-game unbeaten streak of the Pittsburgh Penguins, who played without superstar Mario Lemieux.

The loss was the first for Pittsburgh goaltender Patrick Lalime, who set a record by going unbeaten in his first 16 NHL games. "You knew it had to end," he said. "For me, I just have to start over next game."
Colorado played most of the game without All-Star goalie Patrick Roy, who suffered an apparent right hand injury late in the opening period. Craig Billington replaced him and finished with 31 saves.
"It worked out. The guys worked hard, we got the win," Billington said. "We kept them in the seats tonight. It was just a great victory, battling like we did."
Adam Deadmarsh had two goals and two assists for the Avalanche, who squandered a 3-0 third-period lead but improved to 10-1-3 in their last 14 games.
"The first two periods we played very strong," he said. "In the third, I thought we sat back a little bit. Obviously, with their offence that could be a mistake. It almost was tonight."
The game-winner came after referee Paul Devorski was about to call a delayed penalty on Pittsburgh's Ron Francis for pulling down Keith Jones behind the Penguins' net.

But Colorado controlled the puck and Deadmarsh's centering pass deflected off Uwe Krupp in the slot. The puck came to Kamensky at the left goalpost and he lifted it over Lalime for his 17th goal of the season and second game-winner in three games.
Joe Mullen had a goal and an assist for Pittsburgh, which had gone 12-0-2 since December 17.
Lemieux, the league's leading scorer, sat out with back spasms, but is expected back for weekend games against the Rangers and Montreal.
Pittsburgh's Joe Dziedzic sent the game to overtime when he poked his own rebound past Billington with 4:08 remaining.

Ron Francis began the Pittsburgh comeback from a 3-0 deficit 2:42 into the third period with a wrist shot from the edge of the left faceoff circle. Mullen made it 3-2 just 66 seconds later with his 497th career goal.
In St Louis, Brett Hull scored twice in the third period, including the go-ahead goal with 1:14 remaining, as the Blues edged the Vancouver Canucks 4-3 for their third straight win.
The go-ahead goal was the 23rd goal of the season for Hull, who moved into a tie for the league lead with his sixth game-winner.
Hull's first goal of the game broke a 1-1 tie 51 seconds into the third period. But Vancouver surged ahead as Pavel Bure and David Roberts scored in a 24-second span.
Jamie Rivers tied it with 4:44 remaining when he scored his first NHL goal.
Joe Murphy had the other goal for the Blues, who have won four of their last five games and avenged an embarrasing 8-0 home loss to the Canucks on December 15.

In Phoenix, Cliff Ronning had two goals and an assist and Mike Gartner added a pair of power-play tallies as the Coyotes snapped a three-game losing streak with a 6-3 victory over the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim.

Craig Janney and Keith Tkachuk also scored and Oleg Tverdovsky set up three goals for the Coyotes, who won for just the second time in eight games. Phoenix has won all three meetings with the Ducks this season after losing 10 of the first 12 between the clubs.

Paul Kariya recorded his second hat trick in five games and the second of his career for Anaheim, which lost for just the second time in six games. Teemu Selanne had two assists, extending his points streak to 10 games with seven goals and eight assists.
In Boston, Radek Dvorak scored twice and Ray Sheppard had a goal and two assists as the Florida Panthers snapped a season-high three-game losing streak, 4-1 victory over the Bruins.
Rhett Warrener added his first NHL goal for Florida, which vaulted into sole possession of second place in the Atlantic Division, one point ahead of the idle Rangers.
